summary: Any price can change the optimal transaction, so a correct algorithm must inspect all n prices in the worst case. The running-minimum scan processes each price once.

optimality.argument: Suppose an algorithm leaves some price unread. Depending on that day's position, changing it to a sufficiently low legal buy price or sufficiently high legal sale price can change the maximum profit while all inspected prices stay fixed. Exact computation therefore requires Omega(n) inspections in the worst case. The current algorithm performs constant work for each price, giving O(n) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: An unseen price can become an endpoint of the uniquely best legal transaction, so no exact algorithm can skip arbitrary input positions.
The implementation updates a running minimum and best profit once for each price.
The source-fidelity-verified examples cover a profitable transaction and the no-profit outcome; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
